## Foods & dishes
- [[Bahrain Food Composition Tables]]: 83 dish rows (82 dishes per the book) consumed in Bahrain: traditional sweets 20 · vegetables & legumes 13 · sandwiches 13 · meat 12 · seafood 10 · chicken 8 · breads 4 · milk 3. Gulf dishes (machboos, harees, qouzi, balaleet, gemat, rangina, halwa Bahraini) plus Levantine and South Asian foods common in Bahrain.
  - Ingredients with grams are in the book's annex, but the text layer is garbled and was not extracted (amounts: partial); no cooking steps.
- [[WorldCuisines]]: 11 dishes, 0 Bahrain-specific.
- [[FmLAMA]]: 1 dish (34 rows).
- Absent from [[ArabCulture]], [[BLEnD]] and recipe corpora.

## Ingredients & food composition
- **Own FCT:** [[Bahrain Food Composition Tables]], per 100 g: 12 macro columns (incl. SFA/TFA/MUFA, cholesterol), 15 minerals (incl. iodine, selenium), 10 vitamins (incl. D, B12, folate).
  - Only 27 dish rows are MOH lab analyses. About 56 are borrowed: Kuwait 24, Oman 12, Lebanon 12, Jordan 7, UAE 1, so they reflect those countries' recipes.
  - 113 market products (snacks, dairy, beverages, baby food…) with macronutrients.
- Raw ingredients: borrow from [[USDA FoodData Central]].

## Compounds & traditional medicine
- [[KNApSAcK Family]]: 23 records (4 edible / 19 medicinal). No [[CMAUP]] entry, no Duke records.
- For compound → effect chains use the [[Global]] backbones ([[FooDB]], [[CTD]], [[Phenol-Explorer]], [[SpiceRx]], [[DDID]] for food–drug interactions); [[FooDB]] has **no nigella/black seed, sumac, camel milk, za'atar, ghee or labneh**.

## Gaps
- Dish composition is mostly borrowed; no Bahraini recipe corpus, QA data or traditional-medicine data.
